messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quiet-window protocol for annual evaluations: on-call rota & redaction steps

Team —

As we kick off the annual evaluation window next week I want to lock down two things before we publish manager comms: the manager on-call rota (who covers urgent requests during silent/quiet windows) and the redaction workflow for any privileged cases. I sketched a lightweight approach attached (quiet_window_checklist_v1.pdf). Key asks: 

- Can ops corps confirm the on-call coverage model (a 1-week rotating primary + secondary) is operationally feasible?
- Can compliance confirm the minimum redaction granularity (names + emails + content snippets) so managers know what to remove from shared summaries?
- I want a short manager-facing template we can drop into Confluence Friday so managers have a single place to reference.

Proposed timeline:
- Thu 6/10: internal review + feedback
- Fri 6/11: finalize on-call rota + redaction guidance
- Mon 6/14: publish manager comm + central drive folder

Attachment: quiet_window_checklist_v1.pdf (checklist + quick flow)

Thanks — please reply inline.

Jordan
Jordan Blake
Director, People Operations
Redwood Inference

This looks good. A couple notes:
- On-call model: ops can support the 1-week primary / secondary approach but we should add an escalation policy for payroll/comp exceptions — I'll draft the extra step.
- Manager load: for teams with >30 heads we'll provide a manager buddy for redaction review (peer check) to avoid mistakes.
- Communications: recommend two comms, one short "what to expect" and a separate detailed checklist. The short note should go to managers only; the detailed checklist (with redaction rules) into Drive.

Attachments: manager_oncall_rota_v2.xlsx (rota + tentative names)

Laura Bennett
VP, People Programs
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Quiet-window protocol for annual evaluations: on-call rota & redaction steps

Jordan / Laura —

Thanks for the draft. A few compliance-critical items to include in the redaction SOP (I've attached a short guidance doc):

- Minimum redaction scope: redact full names, personal email addresses, personal phone numbers, government IDs; summarize role/impact rather than copying free-text comments that contain PII.
- Preserve job-relevant context: keep job titles and team-level descriptors when needed for calibration, but remove identifiers that could trace back to individuals.
- Audit trail: any redaction must be recorded in the audit log with redactor name + timestamp; we'll need a separate column in the manager rota sheet to capture who performed redaction.
- Exception path: for legal or accommodation cases, escalate to HR Ops (hr_ops@acme-enterprises.com) and include a second-level reviewer.

Attachment: pii_redaction_guidance.docx (2 pages)

Also: Ellen (cc'd) — can the external compliance review please confirm this granularity is acceptable for SOC2/privacy reviewers?

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Head of Compliance
Redwood Inference
